title: Forced to pick, Grok’s AI model chooses Republicans. OpenAI’s picks Democrats.
slides: Why would an AI have a political party?
Grok tilted Republican when forced to choose a side
OpenAI's model leaned the opposite way on the same test
Your prompts may inherit a hidden partisan default
Test both models on one political question today
thread_text:
1. AI with a party?

Researchers forced Grok to pick a political side—it leaned Republican. The same test on OpenAI's model went the other way.

2. The hidden default

Your prompts may inherit a partisan bias baked into the model. You don't see it until you ask a question with a clear political answer.

3. Two models, two sides

Grok tilted right, OpenAI tilted left—on the exact same question. That's not random; it's a design choice you never voted for.

4. The consequence

If you rely on AI for news or analysis, you're getting a skewed take. The bias is silent, consistent, and scales with every query.

5. Test it yourself

Take one political question and ask both Grok and ChatGPT today. Compare the answers—then decide if you trust either default.
